newsitem.title: USA: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.
newsitem.headline: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef trading was generally lower during most of the period on moderate demand and moderate to heavy offerings, USDA said.
Retail interest was slow at the start of the trading week, improved as the week progressed, but at the lower price levels for immediate needs. Some forward interest was noted late.
Chuck and most round cuts continued to trade lower, while the gooseneck cuts were steady to firm.
Loin cuts also were under pressure, with the most pressure on the top butts and choice tenderloins.

Choice rib cuts were steady, while Select cuts showed some firmness mostly late in the trading week. Closely trimmed items followed somewhat the same pattern as the commodity product, generally trading lower, with the chuck and the round cuts experiencing the most losses.

Beef trimmings traded lower on moderate demand and moderate to heavy offerings. Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items were uneven, fed cattle grinds were lower and the blends generally steady on light to moderate demand.

For the week - Select and Choice rib primal steady to 1.00 higher; Select and Choice chuck primal 2.00 to 3.00 lower; Select and Choice round primal 2.00 lower; Select and Choice loin primal 1.00 to 2.00 lower; Closely trimmed items 1.00 to 2.00 lower; Beef trimmings 1.00 to 1.50 lower; Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items steady to 4.00 lower.

The Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses Dn 1.55 at 101.11; 700/850 Dn 1.41 at 99.60; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses Dn 1.71 at 95.27; 700/850 Dn 1.66 at 94.59.

COW AND BULL CARCASS, BONELESS PROCESSING BEEF, CUTTER COW CUTOUT Temperatures moderated as winter weather conditions improved from recent weeks. This allowed for an increased marketing of slaughter cows in the upper Midwest, which in turn, increased the supply of boneless beef.

At the same time, slaughter cow numbers in the South continue to be limited. However, demand remained light, especially from fast food grinders due to backed up inventories. As a result, boneless beef declined after last week's sharp increase.
Cow carcasses traded steady on moderate demand and offerings. The 100 percent lean items continue to trade at firmer price levels on light offerings.

Utility and Cutter carcasses steady; 90% boneless beef 4.00-5.00 lower; 85% 5.00-6.50 lower; 75% 1.00 lower; 65% 1.50-2.00 lower. The Cutter cow carcass gross cut-out value for Thursday, January 23, 1996 was estimated at 66.85 per cwt., down 2.36 from a week ago Friday.
